question_title: Will the Argentine Senate give final approval to the 'Ley Hojarasca' before August 8, 2026?
summary: The Ley Hojarasca will very likely become law eventually — it has a favorable Senate committee dictamen and a clear governing majority (LLA+PRO+UCR+provincial allies), and passes easily if it reaches the floor. But this question hinges narrowly on whether the definitive Senate floor vote occurs between July 25 and Aug 7. The only plausible in-window session is Aug 6, which is confirmed but dedicated to resuming the contentious property-rights bill (its 5th postponement). The most recent reporting (El Litoral) says Hojarasca has been displaced to Aug 13 — outside the window. The binding constraint is floor time, not votes. Residual YES probability (~15%) comes from genuine schedule ambiguity (Infobae still listed both bills for Aug 6, block leaders had agreed to include it) and the chance the property bill collapses quickly enough that the majority pivots to dispatch the uncontentious Hojarasca while quorum holds.

resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if the Argentine Senate (Honorable Senado de la Nación) passes ("sanciona") the bill known as the "Ley Hojarasca" — the executive-branch bill to derogate obsolete legislation, which entered the Senate as expediente C.D.-1/26 with media sanción from the Chamber of Deputies — in a floor session (sesión) held between July 25, 2026 and August 7, 2026 (inclusive), Argentina local time (UTC−3). Because the bill was passed by the Chamber of Deputies without the Senate proposing amendments, a favorable Senate vote on the unamended text constitutes the definitive sanción of the law. Resolution will be based on the official bill-tracking record for expediente C.D.-1/26 at the Senate's project search portal (https://www.senado.gob.ar/parlamentario/parlamentaria/), which shows the bill's status and any "sanción" entry, or on [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). It resolves NO if no such vote occurs in that window (for example, if the item is postponed, rejected, or not reached).
fine_print: If the Senate approves the bill with amendments and returns it to the Chamber of Deputies (rather than granting definitive sanción), the question resolves NO, since that would not constitute final approval of the law. A vote to reject the bill also resolves NO.

revision_history.reviewer_assessment:
I verified all five factors against the research trace. Every factor's core claim is grounded:

- **Factor 1** (El Litoral: Hojarasca displaced to Aug 13): Supported. The El Litoral article and its WebFetch extraction explicitly state "Ley Hojarasca postponed/displaced to August 13" (trace lines 236, 582, 643).
- **Factor 2** (Aug 6 confirmed, dedicated to property rights bill via cuarto intermedio): Supported. Multiple sources confirm the Aug 6 session is the resumption of the property-rights cuarto intermedio (lines 571-582, 607).
- **Factor 3** (property bill postponed 5 times): Supported. "Fifth postponement since March 27" (lines 575, 606).
- **Factor 4** (favorable dictamen, LLA+PRO+UCR+provincial majority): Supported. June 17 dictamen, ready for sanción (lines 600, 613).
- **Factor 5** (Infobae July 16 listed both for Aug 6; residual schedule uncertainty): Supported. Infobae's Aug-6 agenda listed both bills (lines 285-289, 610).

No hallucinated evidence, no double-counting, no wrong-direction factors (F1-F3 negative logits align with displacement/floor-time constraints; F4-F5 positive logits align with pass-if-reached and schedule ambiguity). The assessment is internally consistent with the factors.

**Timing check:** Published 2026-07-27, window July 25–Aug 7. All decisive events (Aug 6 session) are forward-looking. No pre-publication-event problem.

**Resolution criteria:** Provided (not missing), citing the Senate bill-tracking portal. The agent engaged with the correct question (whether a definitive floor vote occurs in-window) and correctly noted the amendments/return-to-Deputies path. The agent did NOT fetch the live Senate portal or the Aug 6 temario and openly acknowledged this ("I could not access a live Orden del Día"). This is a data gap, not a criteria misalignment; the forecast doesn't hinge on a specific-source mismatch.

**Probability:** My independent estimate is ~12–20%, centered near 15%. The anchor (~20% base rate for a non-priority scheduled item displaced past a tight window) is reasonable, and the small departure to 15% is justified by the concrete El Litoral displacement reporting — a single real signal, not a pile of soft narrative factors. I have no meaningful disagreement with the 15% estimate.

**Counterargument quality:** Strong. It constructs a coherent 30-35% alternative (block-leader agreement to put Hojarasca on Aug 6, Infobae listing both, uncontentious bill that could be dispatched in minutes if the property bill collapses fast while quorum holds). Not a token gesture. Confidence 0.70 is well-calibrated given the fluid calendar.

This is an inaccurate self-report. It did NOT affect the forecast — the retry returned comprehensive, on-point data — so it does not change direction or magnitude.
